_what: cv15 ring-down spectra for the CORRECT (two_plane ground, the committed leg) and the issue-#740 PRE-FIX (one_plane ground) realizations, both built through cv15's PRODUCTION builder `build_rfx_sim(two_plane=...)` and extracted through its production `_harminv_f0()`.
_why: This fixture is the EVIDENCE for the scope limit pre-declared in docs/design_notes/20260901_patch_mode_identification_predeclaration.md section 5: the #740 vacuum ground cell rescales the whole cavity spectrum by a near-common factor (see measured_common_mode_dilation), so it moves every identification residual by that factor and stays inside the derived identification tolerance -- the mode-resolved gate PASSES on it. The audit's proposed mode-pair RATIO band is a separate question and is settled in cv15_mode_pair_ratio_band.json, NOT here: the ratio does move, and the admissible band widths are enumerated there. #740's detector is assert_realized_stack (PR #768), whose exact refusal is recorded below. Keeping the numbers committed means every claim above can be refuted without a solve.

two_plane_ground.source: cv15 build_rfx_sim(two_plane=True) at repo commit 5b6db32, num_periods=45.0 n_freqs=181 --gain (the committed leg's own command). The committed leg validation/crossval/_15_patch_results/rfx.json carries no mode list; its f_harminv_hz agrees with this run's to better than 1e-7 relative -- bound asserted by tests/crossval/test_patch_mode_identification.py::test_cv15_reproduction_ringdown_matches_the_committed_leg

one_plane_ground_740_defect.assert_realized_stack: RuntimeError: assert_realized_stack: realized electric-wall plane(s) do not match the declared stack -- no electric wall at z_sub_lo=7.9375 mm (k=18, ok=False) and/or z_sub_hi=11.1125 mm (k=22, ok=True); realized full-footprint wall planes at k=[17, 22] (z~[13.4937, 17.4625] mm, pad included). Refuse to quote f0 for a cavity taller than the declared substrate (issue #740).

measured_common_mode_dilation.note: the three modes dilate by a nearly common factor (mean 1.068090, half-spread 0.002299), so the defect is close to a pure dilation; but NOT exactly one: the TM_pair ratio moves by -0.1934 % (cv15_mode_pair_ratio_band.json::measured_anchored_band.defect_offset_from_correct_build), which is why a ratio band with a derivable half-width CAN in principle separate it (admissible_interval_is_nonempty = true) -- the round-1 sentence 'every dimensionless spectral observable is blind to it' was an over-statement, withdrawn in the design note 6.9. What blocks a ratio band is not blindness but that no half-width can be derived that admits the correct build and rejects #740 with margin on this mesh; cv15 lands as a STOP for that reason.
